album: You're Gonna Need A Little Music
label: Republic Records
release_notes: Produced by Justin Meldal-Johnsen (Beck, St. Vincent, Nine Inch Nails); finished at his Los Angeles studio.
Critics call it their most melodic and groove-driven set, with less of the earlier sneer.
Single Redeemer. NACC #41 the week of Oct. 1. Six of 11 tracks carry FCC words.
Recorded between Leeds and Los Angeles. No guest artists found (NME). Outlets differ on label: Republic (Under the Radar) or Island.
draft_comment: Yard Act trade some of the sneer for groove, and it works. Dance-punk you can actually dance to. Lots of FCCs, sadly.

tracks.title: Empty Pledges
tracks.notes: Opener; single with official and lyric videos. Treble calls it the record's full-fledged rap moment.

tracks.title: New Beginnings
tracks.notes: Second single with video, June 23, 2026 (Stereogum). Rolling Stone cites muscular guitars and a shout-along chorus.

tracks.title: Fiction
tracks.notes: NME calls its hook repetitive. Producer ran a drum machine through the vocals (Apple Music). Line of Best Fit: vocals battle Sam Shipstone's crunching riffs.

tracks.title: You're Gonna Need A Little Music
tracks.notes: NME cites a euphoric chorus. Rolling Stone: it glides where New Beginnings surges. Lyric video on YouTube.

tracks.title: Cherophobe Rock
tracks.notes: Some reviewers call it the generic one. Title nods to cherophobe, fear of happiness (Treble). DIY notes crunching vocals.

tracks.title: Thrill Of The Chase
tracks.notes: Apple Music: a drum 'n' bass groove slowed down, with live drums and James Brown-style guitars. Rolling Stone calls it arguably the strongest track.

tracks.title: Janey Said
tracks.notes: Apple Music calls it the heart of the album. Mojo calls it a mournful Streets shuffle.

tracks.title: Redeemer
tracks.notes: Lead single with video; announced the album May 7, 2026 (Our Culture). BrooklynVegan calls it smouldering and bluesy, the most rock Yard Act have sounded.

tracks.title: Talky Talky People
tracks.notes: DIY compares the mood to a Blur B-side.

tracks.title: Over The Barrel
tracks.notes: Barroom piano and a big indie-rock chorus, ending in a rush of noise (New Noise).
